requested_part_assessment.actual_requested_clause: May the two players interleave Gather and Damage?

grades.reason: The full Gather-and-Damage sequence must finish per player; both answers prohibit the proposed interleaving. Choosing the first player is unasked background.

requested_part_assessment.actual_requested_clause: Cleanup or outcome check first?

fact_assessments.expected: Correct the illegal position after the completed action tree but before checking victory/defeat; check the cleaned-up state.

passages.quote: **After the primary action and all triggered actions finish**, remaining illegal humans are cleaned up to the nearest legal land.

grades.reason: Both answers place cleanup after the completed action tree and before the outcome check. Nearest-land and non-action details are correct contextual additions, not extra requirements.

requested_part_assessment.actual_requested_clause: When the Fast threshold is applied

fact_assessments.expected: Apply the Speed-changing threshold when checking the Innate's Speed/phase, before its ordinary effects rather than waiting until ordinary effect resolution.
fact_assessments.observed: Apply the threshold changing Speed before ordinary effects when checking the phase in which the Innate may be used; it can make the Innate Fast.

passages.quote: Apply a threshold changing Speed, Range or targeting when checking that attribute, before the ordinary effects: for example, Thunderspeaker's met Fast threshold permits using its Innate in Fast.

grades.reason: Both apply the Speed change at the phase/Speed check before ordinary effects and allow Fast use under the stipulated met thresholds.

requested_part_assessment.actual_requested_clause: Source and real-versus-nightmare Damage

fact_assessments.expected: The delayed trigger remains Bringer's Power, follows To Dream a Thousand Deaths and deals hypothetical rather than real Damage; the other Spirit causing the trigger does not take ownership.
fact_assessments.observed: The triggered Damage still belongs to Bringer’s Vengeance and follows To Dream a Thousand Deaths, even though another Spirit caused the triggering destruction.

passages.quote: The triggered effect still belongs to the Spirit that used Vengeance: if Bringer used it, its later Damage follows To Dream a Thousand Deaths even when another Spirit's action caused the triggering destruction.
Its Powers' explicit Damage/Destroy cannot actually harm Invaders/Dahan or destroy anything except its own Presence.

grades.reason: Both expressly retain ownership by Bringer and apply To Dream a Thousand Deaths despite the other Spirit triggering it. Naming that rule resolves the hypothetical-versus-real choice; the complete summary defines its no-real-Damage effect. Fear values and piece-type lists are unasked.

requested_part_assessment.actual_requested_clause: Does the Ravage payment cover the later Build?

fact_assessments.expected: No; the first payment skips only the Ravage, not the later Build.
fact_assessments.observed: Yes. First use loses one disk from three, leaving a two-disk Sacred Site. Build requires a fresh optional decision and another disk; that second use is legal while the two-disk site remains, then leaves one disk (no longer a site).

passages.quote: Each use skips just that Ravage or Build action and costs one of Green's Presence in its Sacred Site there.

requested_part_assessment.actual_requested_clause: Decision and cost for the later Build

requested_part_assessment.actual_requested_clause: Is the remaining Sacred Site sufficient?

grades.reason: Both apply the per-Power, per-Invader cap, so moving the same Town into another Tsunami-affected land does not yield a second nightmare destruction. Its numerical Fear conversion and Repeat contrast are unasked.

requested_part_assessment.actual_requested_clause: Does the repeated explicit effect-text Element grant happen again?

fact_assessments.expected: The Repeat resolves Elemental Boon’s explicit Element-grant effect again.
fact_assessments.observed: Yes. A repeated effect that explicitly grants Elements grants those Elements again.

passages.quote: A repeated effect explicitly granting Elements grants those again.

grades.reason: Both expressly grant the effect-text Elements again on Repeat. Printed margin Elements and Powerstorm payment are not requested.

requested_part_assessment.actual_requested_clause: Who may set the Spirit Phase time limit?

fact_assessments.expected: Any player may set that Spirit Phase time limit; it is not reserved for the owner/organizer.
fact_assessments.observed: Any player may set a limit on the time available to complete the Spirit Phase.

passages.quote: **The Urgency of War:** Any player may set a limit on the time available to complete the Spirit Phase, using a timer, a stated condition, or another method.

grades.reason: Both grant the time-limit permission to any player. No unsupported automatic consequence is claimed.

requested_part_assessment.actual_requested_clause: Bringer uses Spirits May Yet Dream to turn an unearned Fear Card in the Fear deck face-up. Does turning it face-up immediately earn that card or let players resolve its Fear effect now, or must it still be earned and resolved normally?

fact_assessments.expected: Turning the card face-up does not itself earn the card.
fact_assessments.observed: No. Turning it face-up only previews it; it is not earned or resolved early. Normal earning and resolution still apply.

passages.quote: This only previews the card: turning it face-up neither earns it nor resolves its Fear effect early; normal earning and resolution still apply.

fact_assessments.expected: Turning it face-up does not resolve its Fear effect or grant early resolution; normal earning and resolution still apply.
fact_assessments.observed: No. Turning it face-up only previews it; it is not earned or resolved early. Normal earning and resolution still apply.

passages.quote: This only previews the card: turning it face-up neither earns it nor resolves its Fear effect early; normal earning and resolution still apply.

grades.reason: Both distinguish previewing from earning and resolving, deny both immediate earning and early resolution, and retain normal earning/resolution.
